headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: Perplexity uploads user documents and browsing context while Pathway is a local document-processing engine with no host isolation or write controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pathway has no clipboard, MCP, browser, or filesystem read/write surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest Perplexity output by default. Perplexity does browse and summarize external content, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or automatic handoff. The only plausible bridge is manual transfer, which keeps this low.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Perplexity output into Pathway inputs, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting untrusted Perplexity text into Pathway pipelines.
Add a human review step before any downstream automation.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity explicitly handles uploaded documents and browsing context, while Pathway is a document-processing system with no host isolation or network egress. Even though Pathway itself shows no file read capability, the pair can still expose sensitive document content if operators move files from Pathway into Perplexity for analysis. The interaction is indirect but plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF documents processed by Pathway are uploaded to Perplexity, those contents enter Perplexity's vendor-hosted context.
IF the same sensitive document set is reused across both agents, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not upload sensitive documents to Perplexity.
Use redacted samples when testing the pair.
Separate document sets by sensitivity.
Review Perplexity privacy settings before use.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on uploads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pathway cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or use MCP, and Perplexity likewise cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. With no overlapping write surface to the same mutable resource, there is no credible capability conflict pathway in the profiles provided.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted shared write access to the same directory or git repo, conflict risk would appear.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only with respect to shared artifacts.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repository.
Use separate output directories.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable storage is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity produces cited answers and browsing-derived summaries, and Pathway is a data-processing engine that could consume those outputs as inputs. The pair therefore supports a plausible chain where Perplexity's unverified synthesis is treated as authoritative by Pathway-driven workflows. No verification step is documented, so the interaction is risky but not inherently action-taking.
conditions: IF Pathway ingests Perplexity-generated text as trusted input, downstream transformations can propagate errors.
IF an operator uses Perplexity output as a source of truth without validation, cascading mistakes increase.
mitigations: Require human verification of Perplexity outputs.
Mark Perplexity-derived fields as untrusted.
Add schema checks before Pathway ingestion.
Compare against primary sources before automation.
requires-engineering: implement citation validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and processes uploaded documents and browsing context, while Pathway is an open-source document-processing tool with no stated residency or retention controls. The pair can therefore create a compliance mismatch when regulated documents are moved into Perplexity's hosted environment. Pathway alone is not the issue; the risk arises from the pairwise data flow into Perplexity.
conditions: IF regulated documents or personal data are uploaded to Perplexity, residency and retention obligations may be implicated.
IF the deployment requires on-prem-only processing, the hosted Perplexity leg violates that constraint.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Perplexity.
Use anonymized or synthetic inputs.
Document data-flow boundaries.
Review vendor privacy terms before deployment.
requires-engineering: route sensitive workloads to an approved on-prem alternative.
